A non-stenosed AV valve, excluding MR and AR

questions.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions

questions.exp: The three arms read physiological excessive rapid filling into a hypercompliant ventricle across a normal AV valve in the young, athletes and hyperkinetic states; increased end systolic volume seen in LV/RV failure, the commonest setting; and less than normal filling of a hypertrophic non-compliant ventricle in LVH, RVH and RCMP. (Book p303)

questions.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions

opts: Pathological S3 occurs earlier than physiological S3; it is heard in MS and AR, but not in MR or AS
Pathological S3 occurs later than physiological S3; it is heard in MR with or without LVF and in severe AS from LVH, but not in MS or AR with LVF
Pathological S3 occurs earlier than physiological S3; it is heard only in MS and TS
Pathological S3 occurs earlier than physiological S3; it is heard in MR with or without LVF and in severe AS from LVH, but not in MS or AR with LVF
questions.exp: The line reads 'Pathological S3 occurs earlier than physiological S3', and the valvular diagram prints MR heard with or without LVF, AS seen in severe AS, MS not seen and AR not seen except with LVF. (Book p303)

questions.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions

S3 is also called the ventricular or protodiastolic gallop
S3 is a high pitched early systolic sound heard with the diaphragm
S3 is not seen in mitral stenosis or tricuspid stenosis

questions.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions

Physiological — excessive rapid filling into a hypercompliant ventricle
Pathological — less than normal filling of a hypertrophic non-compliant ventricle
Pathological — rapid filling across a stenosed AV valve
questions.exp: The three mechanisms are physiological excessive rapid filling into a hypercompliant ventricle in the young or athletic, increased end systolic volume in a dilated ventricle (LVF, MR, AR) and less than normal filling of a hypertrophic non-compliant ventricle (LVH, RVH, RCMP); a stenosed AV valve precludes S3. (Book p303)

questions.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

In the left lateral position at the apex; it does not vary with respiration, and a physiological S3 disappears in the upright position
In the supine position at the apex; it varies with respiration, and a physiological S3 appears only in the upright position
In the left lateral position at the apex; it varies with inspiration, and a physiological S3 disappears in the upright position

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

It reduces venous return so that S3 disappears even if it was heard in the left lateral position
It augments venous return so that a pericardial knock appears in constrictive pericarditis
It augments venous return so that S3 is heard even if it was not heard in the left lateral position
questions.exp: The arrow reads 'Passive leg raising: Augments venous return → S3 heard even if not heard in left lateral', a bedside trick to unmask the sound. (Book p304)

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

MS, TS and constrictive pericarditis

MS, MR and pericardial tamponade

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

Ventricular or presystolic gallop, seen in atrial systole and correlating with the V-wave in the JVP

questions.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table

Atrial contraction increases LV end-diastolic fibre length; it is not seen in MS, MR or AR, but is heard in AS

A raised left ventricular pressure with thickened leaflets causes a sudden doming motion of the valves into the LA
A raised left atrial pressure with thinned leaflets causes a gradual doming motion of the valves into the LV
A raised left atrial pressure with thickened leaflets causes a sudden doming motion of the valves into the LV

questions.sec: The Three S4 Settings, the Opening Snap in Mitral Stenosis with Its S2-OS Interval Ladder and Auscultation Rules, and the Low Pitched Tumour Plop of Atrial Myxoma

It opens the AV valves earlier, so the opening snap comes earlier and the S2–OS interval shortens; S2–OS is inversely proportional to LAP
It opens the AV valves earlier, so the opening snap comes earlier and the S2–OS interval lengthens; S2–OS is directly proportional to LAP

questions.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
questions.q: Which chain is printed for the mitral valve prolapse click during standing or Valsalva?
opts: ↓ afterload → ↑ ventricular cavity size → ↓ stretching of chordae → ↑ prolapse → click moves closer to S2
↓ preload → ↓ ventricular cavity size → ↓ stretching of chordae → ↑ prolapse → click moves closer to S1
↑ preload → ↑ ventricular cavity size → ↑ stretching of chordae → ↑ prolapse → click moves closer to S1
↓ preload → ↓ ventricular cavity size → ↑ stretching of chordae → ↓ prolapse → click moves away from S1
questions.exp: The loop reads standing/Valsalva → ↓ preload → ↓ ventricular cavity size → ↓ stretching of chordae → ↑ prolapse → 'Click moves closer to S1'. (Book p306)

questions.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
questions.q: A young woman has a mid-systolic click and late systolic murmur that move earlier in standing and later on squatting. Which printed mechanism explains the movement?
opts: Standing lowers preload, reducing ventricular cavity size and chordal stretch, so prolapse occurs earlier and the click approaches S1
Standing lowers afterload, increasing ventricular cavity size and chordal stretch, so prolapse occurs earlier and the click approaches S1
Standing lowers preload, reducing ventricular cavity size and chordal stretch, so prolapse occurs later and the click approaches S2
Standing raises preload, increasing ventricular cavity size and chordal stretch, so prolapse occurs later and the click approaches S2
questions.exp: The printed loop is ↓ preload → ↓ ventricular cavity size → ↓ stretching of chordae → ↑ prolapse → click closer to S1, the behaviour that marks a non-ejection click of mitral valve prolapse. (Book p306)

questions.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE about ejection clicks on page 306.
opts: False — they are never confused with a heart sound and vary widely with respiration
False — they are absent in mild stenosis because of calcification
True — they are often confused with a loud S2 and do vary with respiration
True — they are often confused with a loud S1 and do not vary with respiration
questions.exp: The features print 'Often confused with loud S1' and 'Does not vary with respiration', while calcification abolishes the click only in severe stenosis. (Book p306)

questions.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
questions.q: A patient with severe calcific aortic stenosis has no ejection click. What does page 306 say about that?
opts: The click is loudest in severe stenosis because of calcification
The click is absent in severe stenosis because of calcification
The absence of a click excludes aortic stenosis
The click is absent because vascular rather than valvular pathology is present
questions.exp: Under features, 'Absent in severe stenosis (d/t calcification)' is printed first, so a missing click does not exclude severe disease. (Book p306)

questions.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — three are printed features of ejection clicks, one belongs to the non-ejection click of mitral valve prolapse:
opts: It moves closer to S1 on standing because of reduced preload
It is often confused with a loud S1
It does not vary with respiration
It is heard best in the aortic area
questions.exp: Movement with standing is the dynamic auscultation of the non-ejection click of mitral valve prolapse; ejection clicks are confused with loud S1, do not vary with respiration and are best heard in the aortic area. (Book p306)

units.title: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions
units.sec: The Diastolic Continuation from Protodiastole to Atrial Systole, the O-P-Time-S3-S4 Sequence, Early, Mid and Late Diastolic Position, and S3 with Its Three Mechanisms and Four Valve Lesions
units.guide:
The cycle continues (p303) from protodiastole through closed semilunar valves, isovolumetric relaxation, opening AV valves, rapid and reduced filling (70% passive) to atrial systole (30% active).
Diastolic sounds run opening snap, pericardial knock and tumour plop as early diastolic, S3 mid diastolic and S4 late diastolic, with S3, S4 and tumour plop the low pitched ones.
S3 is the ventricular or protodiastolic gallop of rapid filling, requiring a non-stenosed AV valve and so absent in MS and TS; its mechanisms are physiological hypercompliant filling in the young, increased end systolic volume in LV/RV failure, and reduced filling of a hypertrophic non-compliant ventricle in LVH, RVH and RCMP, with pathological S3 earlier than physiological; it is heard in MR and severe AS but not MS or AR.

units.title: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table
units.sec: S3 Features with Left Lateral Position, Leg Raising and the Heart-Failure Caveat, the Pericardial Knock of Constrictive Pericarditis, and S4 with Its Four Prerequisites and Its Valve-Disease Table
units.guide:
S3 is heard in the left lateral position at the apex, does not vary with respiration, disappears upright when physiological, and appears with passive leg raising; heart failure without S3 means MS, TS or pericardial tamponade (p304).
The pericardial knock of chronic constrictive pericarditis is high pitched, louder with inspiration and early diastolic, increasing with cardiac output and disappearing after pericardiectomy.
S4 is the atrial or presystolic gallop of atrial systole correlating with the JVP A-wave, needing healthy atria in sinus rhythm contracting vigorously across a non-stenosed AV valve into a non-dilated ± hypertrophic non-compliant ventricle; its mechanism is a rise in LV end-diastolic fibre length, and it is not seen in MS, MR or AR but is heard in AS, and in acute MR and AR; the table gives AS +/+, AR in failure/–, MS –/– and MR +/–.

units.title: The Three S4 Settings, the Opening Snap in Mitral Stenosis with Its S2-OS Interval Ladder and Auscultation Rules, and the Low Pitched Tumour Plop of Atrial Myxoma
units.sec: The Three S4 Settings, the Opening Snap in Mitral Stenosis with Its S2-OS Interval Ladder and Auscultation Rules, and the Low Pitched Tumour Plop of Atrial Myxoma
units.guide:
S4 also appears with concentric LVH from systemic HTN or HCM, concentric RVH from PS, PAH or RCM, and RV ischaemia from coronary disease (p305).
The opening snap is AV valve opening representing isovolumetric relaxation, heard with the bell at the apex in expiration, requiring mobile leaflets, good LV function and organic MS as the predominant lesion; raised LAP with thickened leaflets causes sudden doming, so OS α LAP and S2–OS α 1/LAP, printing S2–OS >120 mmHg with LAP <5 mmHg in mild disease and 40–60 mmHg with LAP >15 mmHg in severe disease.
It is heard standing midway between apex and lower left sternal border and does not vary with respiration; tumour plop is low pitched, from atrial myxoma, and early diastolic.

units.title: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
units.sec: Systolic Added Sounds as Clicks, the Valvular and Vascular Ejection Clicks with Their S2 and S1 Rules, and the Non-Ejection Click of Mitral Valve Prolapse with Dynamic Auscultation
units.guide:
Systolic added sounds are clicks, split into ejection clicks (valvular and vascular) and non-ejection clicks (p306).
Ejection clicks come from semilunar valve opening: valvular clicks from a doming valve halted abruptly in AS, PS and bicuspid aortic valve, and vascular clicks from sudden distension beyond the valve in aneurysm; root pathology loudens S2 while valvular pathology softens it, fever with tachycardia loudens S1.
Ejection clicks disappear in severe calcific stenosis, are best heard in the aortic area, are often confused with a loud S1, do not vary with respiration, and a pulmonary click is better heard in expiration; non-ejection clicks belong to mitral valve prolapse, where standing or Valsalva lowers preload, shrinks the cavity, reduces chordal stretch, increases prolapse and moves the click toward S1.
